top.title: Usman Khawaja says 'I haven't thrown anyone under the bus' after ball-tampering revelations
top.description: Usman Khawaja has denied throwing anyone under the bus after making explosive claims about the infamous ‘Sandpaper-gate’ scandal in his new book. Khawaja, who retired after last winter’s Ashes, wrote in extracts in his autobiography Sabr , which is set to be published on Tuesday, that the entire Australia team knew about the plot to use sandpaper to tamper with the ball during a Test match against South Africa in Cape Town 2018. At the time only captain Steve Smith, deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught on television cameras applying the sandpaper, took responsibility for the scheme. The former two received one-year bans while Bancroft was suspended for nine months. Khawaja said that captain Steve Smith talked him out of insisting the entire team take responsibility and also alleged that a member of the coaching staff encouraged Bancroft. Khawaja said in a two-part video statement on Instagram: “I haven’t thrown anyone under the bus. These three guys took the blame for all of us and they’re the victims. The truth has never come out. “I stayed quiet yesterday but if you read my article you’d have seen, when I said it was all of us, that’s implying that whether we like it or not we are all responsible for what happened together. As a team, we need to take that collectively. Am I going to deny that everyone knew? No. “But I never speak on behalf of anyone else in my book – contrary to what the headlines in clickbait media would have you think. “The only other thing that I think is really relevant, which I want to talk about, is the question why now? Well, because I’ve been trying to take this as a team right from the start. You can believe my story or not.” Khawaja added: “When the other guys got their penalties I told Smudge (Smith) that I was going to come clean to the media. I couldn’t believe the penalty he got, but Smudge being the man and leader he was talked me out of it. “He wanted to take the blame. I argued with him, but he was having none of it.” Khawaja said “all of us” knew about the plot and said that he had again wanted to come clean in 2021, before a statement was released by now-captain Pat Cummins and the rest of the bowling unit, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon in which they denied any involvement. “I wasn’t going to go to war with those guys,” Khawaja said. As for why he had waited until now to finally speak out, he said: “Call me a chicken or whatever you want. I didn’t know how to do it because I was still in the team. I was always conscious of putting my team first, but I’m not in that team anymore. What I say now isn’t a reflection of them anymore.” The book is also expected to allege that the same tactic was first used in the previous Test at Gqeberha. Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann denied Khawaja’s claims of widespread knowledge of the plot, but acknowledged that ball-tampering was a “big part” of international cricket during the period. top.title: Walsh-inspired Australia crush irate Samoa to reach World Cup final
top.description: Reece Walsh (left) celebrated his first try with a spectacular backflip in Sydney [Getty Images] Australia (26) 44 Tries: Walsh 3, Dearden, Preston, Trbojevic, Best, Bostock Goals: Munster 6 Samoa (2) 12 Tries: Crichton, Tago Goal: Crichton Penalty: Crichton Before kick-off, Samoa's ceremonial war dance - the Siva Tau - turned into an intense face-off, with their players going right into the faces of their Australian opponents, and a couple even going forehead to forehead. It turned out to be the closest Samoa got to Australia all evening. Australia dominated at Sydney Football Stadium, triumphing 44-12 to reach a 16th successive men's Rugby League World Cup final. In a repeat of the previous World Cup final, a worked-up Samoa side lost their way with errors and ill-discipline, allowing Australia to run in eight tries, including a Reece Walsh hat-trick. Australia - who have won the past three world titles in a row - will face New Zealand in Brisbane next Sunday with kick-off at 08:35 GMT. Walsh hat-trick helps Australia into RL World Cup final - as it happened Samoa had taken the lead after three minutes when Stephen Crichton – whose golden-point drop goal beat England in the 2022 semi-final – landed a penalty in front of the posts. But Australia led soon after when Tom Dearden picked up from a scrum and blasted through the non-existent line to score. Australia's next two tries came after they got six again thanks to poor Samoa discipline. Jacob Preston burst under the posts on 15 minutes; 10 minutes later, joint-top World Cup scorer Tom Trbojevic scored his eighth try of the tournament, benefiting after Crichton reached into the ruck. Walsh got in on the party - celebrating with a backflip - and the scoring was topped before half-time when Bradman Best bounced off tackles and into the corner. Both sides were fired up by regional rivalry, as the Siva Tau showed pre-match. Samoa's Brian To'o leaned his forehead into the face of Tino Fa'asuamaleaui, the Australia prop who played for Samoa in 2019. But Samoa's passion dissolved into frustration as the game got away - not helped by some questionable refereeing decisions. The most egregious came on the half-hour, when Crichton appeared to have grounded to close the score to 16-6 after Francis Manuleleua had beaten Walsh to a high ball. But a slow-motion replay led to the debatable conclusion Manuleleua had knocked on. It was the final straw for some Samoa players - Spencer Leniu was sin-binned for speaking out of turn to referee Adam Gee just before the break. Crichton did get his try in the second half after Walsh dropped a bomb, and Isack Tago scored in the corner with 18 minutes left But Walsh quickly responded after both Samoan scores, keeping them at arm's length while scoring his first international hat-trick. Bostock added gloss with eight to go. The damage was done - mostly by Samoa to themselves. Matt's player of the match: Jacob Preston I loved the industry and punch of Jacob Preston's work

top.title: Late release, upright seam, heavy ball: Decoding Mohammed Shami’s sorcery
top.description: Few bowlers possessed the ability to strip a batter of his technique, judgement, and ego like Mohammed Shami. The fast bowler from a nondescript village in Uttar Pradesh’s Sahaspur, which literally translates to the “land of courage”, bowled with a big heart, indefatigable spirit, and unmatched skill over 64 Tests. Former England captain Alastair Cook’s dismissal during the Visakhapatnam Test in 2016 was a case in point. Shami bowled a series of outswingers that forced Cook to play away from his body. On cue, he then delivered a perfect inswinger that jagged back sharply to sneak past Cook's defence and cannon onto the stumps. “It’s all in those beautiful wrists,” Shami’s childhood coach Badruddin Siddiqui told TOI. “The reason for his success was that he released the ball late and did not rush through his action. This helped him extract late swing off the track. With those malleable wrists, he made subtle changes at the point of release that batters found hard to pick,” the coach demystified Shami’s skill set. Like S Sreesanth, Shami possessed one of the most upright, God-gifted seam positions in world cricket. Shami was also a bit of a paradox because of the ability to make the old ball skid low while also hurling the ‘heavy ball’ that flew past the batter’s nose. The ‘heavy ball’ — the delivery that pitches shorter and reaches the batter quicker than expected, and hits the bat with extra force despite bowling from a relatively smooth, upright run-up — became Shami’s calling card on numerous overseas tours. The 2018 Johannesburg Test was a classic example: he dismantled South Africa, cruising at 124/1, for 177 to hand India a landmark 63-run win. Shami finished with figures of 5/28, unleashing his trademark ‘heavy ball’ on the spicy Wanderers pitch. At times, he could be erratic even when the conditions were loaded in his favour. But without any warning, he would return with a magical, match-altering spell against the run of play. This streak of unpredictability made Shami irresistible, and it was instrumental in India winning more matches abroad, especially under Virat Kohli’s captaincy. Shami was also a great senior, who passed on his art and tricks of the trade to youngsters. “I learnt a lot of things from him during my time in the IPL. Subtle things like bowling at the death and with the semi-new ball,” Uttar Pradesh pacer Ankit Rajput said. At 36, Shami had been performing admirably in this Ranji season, picking up 14 wickets in his last three games. Yet, the constant snubs and time away from international cricket had hurt him. “He was trying hard to make a comeback. But after a point, he realised he was not going to get another chance in Tests, which is why he chose to retire,” Badruddin explained. “He wants to play the ODI World Cup next year. The former midfielder feels the north London club are achieving phenomenal results despite not playing at their maximum level. top.title: Deion Sanders contract buyout, salary at Colorado in 2026
top.description: The Colorado Buffaloes continue to rack up inexcusable losses against winnable opponents, despite having a coach paid like one of the best in college football. Those two things typically go on for a long time without any resolution. Will Colorado part ways with Deion Sanders? Who knows, but with each passing loss, most recently a 20-10 defeat to Arizona State in Tempe, the answer to that question gets clearer. Results matter, and over the past two seasons, and truthfully for the better part of his four-year tenure aside from 2024 as head coach, the results have been nowhere close to good enough for the amount of resources poured into the program. For a few weeks now, fans have been wondering what it would take for Colorado to move on from Sanders. Well, it would cost a pretty penny. Deion Sanders' contract details In March 2025, Sanders signed a five-year, $54 million contract extension with Colorado that runs through the 2029 season. His base salary this year is $10.8 million, the fourteenth-highest salary in college football. Needless to say, Colorado is nowhere near the fourteenth-best team in the country, and even if the extension was not just for the on-field product, but also for what Sanders brought to the university and city, those boosts have died down as well. Sanders would make $11 million in 2027, $11 million in 2028 and $12 million in 2029 if he saw out the remaining three years of his deal. Deion Sanders' buyout details Like most coaches, Sanders buyout changes depending on whether he leaves or is fired. Colorado could also work out a deal with Sanders to lower his buyout if both sides want to part ways, but that seems least likely, especially in season. If Sanders is fired before the end of 2026, his buyout would be $25.5 million. In 2027, that number would decrease to $17.25 million. Sanders would owe Colorado $10 million if he left for another job before December 31, 2026. Can Colorado afford Deion Sanders' buyout? The biggest question remains whether Colorado could afford the nearly $26 million buyout, and the short answer is yes. If you factor in that Sanders would be paid around $34 million over the next three seasons if he stays, the buyout ($25.5 million) would actually save the university under $8.5 million ($2.8 million per year). The buyout plus hiring a new head coach at $4-4.5 million per year would be about $37.5-39 million, or about $1.5 million more per year over three seasons. A very doable number if that is the direction CU chooses. If you hire a coach with an even lower annual salary, say a current Group of Six coach, the change could cost less than $1 million a year. top.title: Taylor Swift has reportedly made changes to help Travis Kelce
top.description: Feb 11, 2024; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Recording artist Taylor Swift reacts during the first quarter of Super Bowl LVIII between Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports Taylor Swift has made no secret of her love for baking, and she has even shared her treats with Travis Kelce over the course of their relationship. But now that Kelce is in the middle of what could be his final NFL season, the newlyweds have reportedly made some changes in the kitchen. According to a new report, Swift has cut back on the sweets to help her husband stay in shape. The couple has also reportedly been hitting the gym together and sticking to a strict diet as Kelce tries to keep up with the demands of his 14th season with the Kansas City Chiefs. Kelce’s Final Run? Kelce decided to return to the Chiefs in March after plenty of speculation that he could retire, and many believe that this will be his last season. At 37, he has had to work harder than ever to stay on the field, and head coach Andy Reid has even suggested that the veteran may see a reduced workload . Swift, meanwhile, has been right there with him. The couple got married over the Fourth of July weekend, and Swift has been a regular presence in her suite at Arrowhead Stadium this season. Swift has reportedly fully supported Kelce through the long football season, despite how much of his time it demands. And it sounds like that support extends to their meals at home. Cutting Back on the Sweets According to an insider who spoke to the Daily Mail , Swift has been working out alongside Kelce and has adjusted her diet to fit his training. “They work out a ton together,” the insider said. “They love to lift weights and stay strong, and they stick to a lean diet. There is a lot of protein in their meals.” Swift is known for her love of baking, and she revealed on Kelce’s New Heights podcast in 2025 that the two had gotten into making sourdough bread. She also famously made homemade Pop-Tarts for the Chiefs’ offensive linemen back when she first started dating Travis. But according to the report, Swift has “eased off” on the sweets because Kelce “needs to be in the best shape of his life.” That doesn’t mean she has given up on baking completely. The insider claimed that she still makes Kelce’s “favorite” treat, French toast, from time to time. “When she is with Travis, she does everything to support him because he is working so hard on football,” the insider said. Travis is on the back end of his career and clearly does not have the same athleticism that he had in his prime. That means that he has to work a little harder to make sure he stays in shape, and it sounds like Taylor is committed to helping him do that. top.title: What Steph Curry went and said in the Warriors locker room right after beating Magic 126-119
top.description: Photo by Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images The Golden State Warriors were involved in a thriller against the Orlando Magic. Steve Kerr’s men dominated the first half, winning the first quarter by 12 and the second by four, thus going into the break with a 16-point lead. However, in the third quarter, the Magic outscored the Warriors by 17 points and took the lead. Steph Curry led the comeback in the fourth, and with the game tied at the buzzer, the two teams went to overtime. The Warriors won by seven points in the end, and although Curry was the star of the show, he was beyond impressed by his teammates. Steph Curry’s locker room message to Golden State Warriors teammates after beating Orlando Magic If you just look at the scores and Curry’s stat sheet, you would think that the 38-year-old led his side to victory once again. You wouldn’t be wrong to think that, but what was really interesting at the start of overtime was seeing Kerr leave both Curry and Draymond Green on the bench. That shocked everyone, but the players on the court for the first minute or so helped the Warriors to go up by four points. Curry and Green then came on to finish the job, but seeing the younger guys deliver at such a key moment of the game really impressed the 2022 NBA Finals MVP. After the game, Curry reportedly went to the locker room and heaped praise on his teammates for their performance against the Magic. “Steve Kerr says Steph Curry addressed the team in the locker room tonight to tell them how much he trusts this group and gave praise to the bench and depth,” Dalton Johnson reported live on X. In his press conference , Kerr said: “He spoke to the team after the game about the contributions of the bench, and he mentioned how much trust that he and the vets have in the young guys. “So, we’ve got a good thing going.” Curry is absolutely right to praise his teammates. Leaving him and Green out for the first minute could’ve easily backfired, but the fact that it didn’t shows the quality of the depth. That is one of the reasons why the Warriors have now won seven games in a row.

top.title: BEDC announces salary increase for staff
top.description: Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) Plc has announced salary increases for all staff following an agreement with two recognised labour unions, effective Dec. 1. This is contained in a statement issued by the management of the electricity distribution firm on Sunday in Benin. The agreement was reached at a meeting between the company’s management, the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) and the Senior Staff Association of Electricity and Allied Companies (SSAEAC) on Nov. 6. The meeting was led by BEDC’s Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Jonathan Lawani. SSAEAC was represented by its Deputy General Secretary, Comrade Innocent Lord-Douglas, while NUEE was represented by Comrade Mbang Ntukubes. Lawani, in the statement, said the successful conclusion of negotiations, which began in March, demonstrated management’s commitment to staff welfare and improved organisational performance. “The successful conclusion of this joint negotiation and review process reflects our shared commitment to staff welfare and the overall performance of BEDC,” he said. He, however, described the recent industrial action by workers as avoidable, saying it resulted in revenue losses, reputational damage and hardship for electricity consumers. Lawani expressed regret that the industrial action occurred before the agreed date for concluding negotiations, as reaffirmed at the Oct. 7 meeting. He also explained that BEDC’s approved operational expenditure framework had remained fundamentally unchanged since 2013, in spite of rising costs and prevailing economic realities. According to him, access to the company’s full approved operational expenditure allocation depends on meeting prescribed collection performance thresholds, while shortfalls result in reduced allocations. The management said the explanation underscored the company’s financial constraints and the need to balance employees’ welfare with business sustainability. BEDC commended the leadership of NUEE and SSAEAC for their cooperation and constructive engagement in reaching an amicable resolution. The company reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, mutual respect and industrial harmony, describing employee welfare as central to its transformation agenda. It said the agreement represented a step towards strengthening trust, collaboration and shared responsibility between management and organised labour The post BEDC announces salary increase for staff appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.description: Several F1 drivers slammed the full wet tire after São Paulo GP qualifying, saying it lacked grip in standing water and the intermediate was better. F1 cars rarely run on the full wet tire, which made São Paulo GP qualifying a rare test, and many F1 drivers told the media afterward that they weren’t happy with the grip in such tricky conditions. Drivers said it took laps to clear the standing water and get the tire working, especially in Q1. Many favored the intermediate, as they did with the previous generation of cars. They expected a tire built for extreme weather to handle it, but said it struggled in standing water. There were several off moments during qualifying, including incidents for home heroes Gabriel Bortoleto and Rafael Camara . Lando Norris took pole, but the grid is jumbled up with several F1 drivers facing penalties. The forecast for Sunday is rain all day, even though there is a possibility of a dry run during the race. top.title: Argyle boss 'excited' as Baidoo marks return with goal
top.description: Baidoo scored his first goal for Plymouth Argyle nearly two years after his £1m move to Home Park [Shutterstock] Plymouth Argyle boss Tom Cleverley says he was impressed by Michael Baidoo's return to action. The Ghana forward, 27, had been out since injuring his hamstring in the final game of pre-season in early August. He came on as a substitute in the 4-0 FA Cup first-round win over non-league Alvechurch , scoring the Pilgrims' third goal - his first for the club. Baidoo was Argyle's record signing when he joined for more than £1m in January 2025 from Swedish side Elfsborg. But he struggled to adapt to life in the Championship and spent last season on loan at Qatari side Umm Salal. "Michael's versatile in terms of where I can play him," Cleverley said. "He's intelligent, he finds the space well, which is something we don't really have as a team. "Then within those small pockets of space, he's really safe with a ball, he can get on the half turn, he can make things happen, he's got explosive speed. "He's a player I'm excited about without putting too much pressure on him, scored another goal to add to his almost a goal a game in pre-season, so a positive day, and the main thing is he's played for his first minutes for a long time and he's come through safe and sound." Plymouth Argyle 4-0 Alvechurch Baidoo to return as Plymouth take no FA Cup chances Cleverley said he was happy his side did not panic despite going in at half-time level at 0-0 with their seventh-tier opponents who play in Southern League Premier Division Central. Will Evans broke the deadlock early in the second half and went on to score a sepond before goals from Baidoo and Ronan Curtis secured the win. "I hope they enjoyed their cup run, they were very well supported," added Cleverley. "I saw one of their directors this morning at breakfast and they were very excited by the day and that's what the FA Cup's about. "We are the so-called giants there to be killed today and if we get through to the third round then the shoe could be on the other foot and we're going somewhere to try to kill a giant "It's the beauty of the cup. nigeria.title: Military hardware: Manufacturer seeks dedicated funding
nigeria.description: The Chairman/CEO of EPAIL Nigeria, Kola Balogun, has called for dedicated government funding and stronger regulatory frameworks to accelerate Nigeria’s indigenous defence manufacturing industry. Balogun said sustainable development of the industry required deliberate government intervention, structured research funding and effective regulation of local manufacturers. He made the call in an interview with Newsman on the just-concluded Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) 2026. He said Nigeria needed a strong regulatory institution to establish standards, monitor research activities and ensure accountability in the utilisation of funds allocated to defence manufacturing. According to him, government funding should be directed towards clearly identified research priorities and solutions to the country’s peculiar security challenges. “We should not merely make budgetary provisions for defence manufacturing without clearly identifying the projects, research priorities and expected outcomes. “Government funding must be purposeful, dedicated and properly monitored.” Balogun argued that competition among indigenous manufacturers should be driven by government-funded research and innovation rather than unhealthy commercial rivalry. He said the government could identify specific security challenges and invite local manufacturers to develop competing technological solutions. “For instance, imagine a situation where we want to detect any object approaching our borders within a specified distance and automatically raise an alarm. “That should become a research challenge for indigenous defence manufacturers,” he said. He explained that manufacturers could receive initial funding to develop different solutions, after which the government would assess the proposals and support the most promising innovations. The EPAIL boss also advocated the establishment of defence industry incubation centres to provide platforms for researchers, engineers and manufacturers to develop and test innovative ideas. “Incubation centres are important because that is where research and innovation can take place. “They provide a clustered environment where individuals, researchers, engineers and companies can bring forward ideas, collaborate and conduct small-scale experiments,” he said. Balogun said the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON) and other relevant institutions should play leading roles in developing such innovation platforms. nigeria.title: Tears, fear as kidnappers invade Enugu community, abduct mother, 3 sons
nigeria.description: A mother and her three sons have been abducted by suspected kidnappers at a farmland in Ugbene Ajima, Uzo-Uwani Local Government Area of Enugu State. The incident reportedly occurred on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at Nwiyi Ivuruge, along the route leading to Umualogo Village in Nkpologu community, a neighbouring community that shares a boundary with Ugbene Ajima. The victims were identified as Mrs Bridget Okey and her three sons, Chukwubuike, Chukwuemeka and Chijioke. One of the children, Chukwubuike, is said to be 14 years old. The family was reportedly harvesting cassava on their farmland when the suspected kidnappers struck, seized the four victims and whisked them away to an unknown destination. The abduction has heightened concerns over the safety of rural residents, particularly farmers, who are increasingly exposed to attacks while carrying out their daily activities. A community leader, Sam Otti, who holds the chieftaincy title of Ikeoha Ugbene, called on the government and security agencies to urgently intervene and secure the victims’ release. Otti said the incident had been reported to local vigilantes, forest guards and the police, while appealing to the Enugu State Government, Uzo-Uwani Local Government Council and other relevant authorities to deploy every necessary resource to rescue the abducted family. He said: “We appeal to the Enugu State Government, Uzo-Uwani Local Government Council, the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to urgently deploy every necessary resource towards securing the immediate and safe release of Mrs Bridget Okey and her three sons. “The family must not be abandoned to its fate. Every possible effort must be made to ensure that the victims return home alive and unharmed. “Subjecting innocent children to the horrors of captivity for financial gain is barbaric and an affront to our collective humanity. No society should tolerate a situation in which children become bargaining chips in the hands of criminal elements. “More troubling is the apparent spread of insecurity into rural communities, where farmers and other residents are increasingly exposed to abduction in places that should ordinarily be safe for their daily activities. “Our farmlands must not become hunting grounds for kidnappers. Our villages must not become safe havens for criminals, and our children must not grow up in fear of accompanying their parents to the farms. “We therefore call on the relevant authorities to act swiftly and decisively. nigeria.title: 5 things to know about Nigeria’s U-17 World Cup-winning coach, Akeem Busari
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup has brought head coach Akeem Ishola Busari into the spotlight after he guided the Flamingos to their first-ever title in the competition. The Nigerian girls defeated Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, 2026, in Morocco, becoming the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Busari’s achievement is particularly remarkable because he was appointed head coach only seven months before the tournament, having inherited a team that had previously finished third at the 2022 edition. Here are five things to know about the coach behind Nigeria’s historic achievement. 1. He is a CAF A-licensed coach Akeem Busari arrives in the role with a long coaching career behind him. A CAF A-licensed coach, he has worked across both men’s and women’s football in Nigeria and abroad, building a reputation for discipline and attacking football. His coaching experience spans more than three decades, with stints at several Nigerian clubs, including Shooting Stars, Gateway United, JSP FC and Bayelsa Queens. He has also worked in the Republic of Benin. 2. He received his coaching training at the National Institute for Sports The Flamingos coach began his formal coaching education at the National Institute for Sports (NIS), Lagos, where he obtained his initial coaching qualification in 1999. According to NIS Director-General Philip Shaibu, Busari subsequently returned to complete the institute’s higher programmes between 2003 and 2006. He received his final coaching certificates in October 2006. His training at the institute preceded his appointment to the national team by nearly two decades. 3. He previously coached several Nigerian clubs Before taking charge of the Flamingos, Busari built his coaching career across several Nigerian clubs. He was head coach of Pacesetter Queens FC in Ibadan before his appointment to the national team. His previous experience also includes working with Shooting Stars, Gateway United, JSP FC and Bayelsa Queens. He played a role in helping Shooting Stars secure promotion to the top flight during the 2008/2009 season. He also won multiple State FA Cup titles with Gateway United and Shooting Stars. In 2023, he guided JSP FC to promotion in the Benin Championship League. He also served as Technical Director of Bayelsa Queens, one of Nigeria’s established women’s football clubs. 4. nigeria.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have rescued 119 civilians abducted by terrorists and recovered eight vehicles during an operation in Borno. According to the report, they engaged the terrorists, forcing them to abandon the abducted civilians and flee in disarray. It said the troops recovered eight vehicles and reunited the rescued civilians with their families. “They also discovered and detonated an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) around the Bam-Buratai Junction-Bulazarma general area. “In a separate development, a suspected fighter of Jama’atu Ahlis-Sunna Lidda’Awati Wal-Jihad (JAS) surrendered to troops of 202 Battalion at Ngurusoye Village, Bama Local Government Area. “The suspect reportedly fled his group’s enclave in Bula Daloye following clashes with the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and hardship. “He surrendered with an FN rifle and seven rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition and is currently in military custody for further action,” it said. The report said troops and members of the Hybrid Force arrested a suspected terrorist informant and collaborator at Ngamdu Town, Borno, on Nov. 5. It added that troops of Army Headquarters Garrison foiled an attempted abduction of a retired senior military officer and his son at Kurudu Phase Five, Abuja. nigeria.title: Inuwa seeks common Northern policy framework to tackle out-of-school children
nigeria.description: Advocates unified regional agenda, investment in agriculture, agro-allied industries to combat poverty, insecurity Sultan applauds Gombe governor’s Almajiri education reforms By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Gombe State Governor and Chairman of the Northern States Governors’ Forum, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has called for a common policy framework and unified regional agenda to sustain education reforms, tackle the growing number of out-of-school children and accelerate human capital development across Northern Nigeria. The governor said addressing the region’s educational challenges required a coordinated approach that went beyond school enrolment to include poverty reduction, improved security, economic empowerment and the creation of sustainable livelihood opportunities for the growing population. Yahaya made the call at the 2026 Biennial Lecture and Awards Ceremony of the Barewa Old Boys Association (BOBA), held in Gombe, with the theme, “The Scourge of Out-of-School Children and the Implications for National Security.” Describing the theme as timely and critical to the future of Northern Nigeria, the governor warned that the increasing number of children outside the formal education system posed serious threats to social stability, economic productivity and national security. He observed that educational exclusion perpetuated poverty, widened inequality and exposed vulnerable children and young people to criminal exploitation, radicalisation and other antisocial tendencies. Yahaya recalled that when his administration assumed office in 2019, Gombe State had more than 500,000 out-of-school children, explaining that sustained interventions by his government had brought approximately 350,000 of them back into the classroom. He attributed the achievement to the declaration of a state of emergency in the education sector, construction of mega schools with expanded learning capacities, recruitment of more than 1,000 qualified teachers and establishment of Almajiri Integrated Learning Centres, among other initiatives. Drawing from the state’s experience, the governor urged Northern states to move away from fragmented interventions and embrace a common regional framework that would identify successful educational models, encourage their adoption across state boundaries and guarantee continuity. He proposed that the Northern States Governors’ Forum should provide the institutional platform for harmonising educational policies, coordinating priorities and strengthening collaboration among the 19 Northern states. According to him, a unified Northern Agenda would ensure that successful programmes initiated by successive administrations were sustained, while promoting the sharing of resources, expertise and best practices for regional development. He maintained that the magnitude of the challenges confronting Northern Nigeria required collective responsibility, stressing that no single state could effectively address the problem of out-of-school children in isolation

nigeria.title: Yoruba started home video, not Nollywood — Osuofia
nigeria.description: Veteran Nollywood actor, Nkem Owoh, popularly known as Osuofia, has clarified his position on the origins of Nigeria’s home-video industry, insisting that Yoruba filmmakers pioneered home-video productions but did not start Nollywood. Owoh made the clarification during an appearance on Curiosity Made Me Ask, hosted by comedian and content creator Adebayo Abidemi, popularly known as Bae U. The interview, published on the host’s YouTube channel on Saturday, featured the actor responding to a question about reports that he had claimed Yoruba people, rather than the Igbo, started Nollywood. The clarification comes amid an ongoing debate over the contributions of different ethnic groups to the development of Nigeria’s film industry. The debate gained fresh attention in August 2026 when late veteran actor Francis Duru argued that the Igbo built Nollywood but that Yoruba filmmakers had become more dominant because of their ability to organise and promote their productions. Duru, who died in October, had attributed much of the growth of the modern home-video industry in the 1990s and early 2000s to Igbo entrepreneurs. Reacting to the reported interpretation of his earlier comments, Owoh said it was inaccurate to suggest that he claimed Yoruba people started Nollywood, explaining that the name did not exist when filmmakers began producing movies. “First of all, you have given me this wrong accusation that I said, Yoruba started Nollywood. No. Yoruba started this film on… when did Nollywood come out? When we started the thing, there was no Nollywood as a name. “We sat together and we’re banding, you know, ideas and all that, how the thing is going to come to fruition. And eventually, we chose Nollywood,” he said. The actor, however, credited Yoruba filmmakers with popularising home-video productions in Nigeria, specifically mentioning veteran filmmaker Hubert Ogunde and Adebayo Papa as among those whose works he admired. “So, Yoruba started the thing. They made the thing very popular home video and all that. Yes, they did. And I’ve said it several. Okay. Ogunde and Adebayo Papa. These are the people I love to watch their thing,” he said. When the interviewer jokingly suggested that Ogunde was Igbo, Owoh disagreed, insisting that the late filmmaker was Yoruba. “Ogunde is not Igbo. I’m telling you that Yoruba started it. When Ogunde was out, I don’t think there was any Igbo man who was that popular in that,” he added. He further emphasised the distinction between the origins of home-video productions and Nollywood, stating: “The Yoruba did not start Nollywood. They started Home video.” Historical accounts of Nigerian cinema trace the development of Yoruba filmmaking to travelling theatre groups led by figures such as Hubert Ogunde and Duro Ladipo, whose stage productions evolved into film and video productions decades before the commercial home-video boom of the 1990s. nigeria.description: Inter Miami’s Lionel Messi won his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday after the defending champions took second place in the Eastern Conference with a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the regular season. The Argentine superstar did not score but set up the first two goals at Miami’s Nu Stadium, both from corners, to help procure his club a home-field advantage for the first two playoff rounds. Messi’s 26 goals this season were enough to make him the first back-to-back MLS Golden Boot award winner. Petar Musa of Dallas was second on 22, not scoring in his club’s 3-1 home victory over Colorado. Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada’s brace soon after the break sparked a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko’s late strike. Runaway overall leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record for a season with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. At 23-3 with eight drawn, Nashville won the East and broke the mark of 74 points set by Miami in 2024. Miami finished second in the East on 60 points as third-place New England failed to take advantage of Inter’s draw with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando to end on 58. Messi’s men will face Columbus to begin the MLS playoffs. Other East matchups send New England against Philadelphia, Charlotte against Chicago and top seed Nashville against the wild-card winner, Orlando or Cincinnati. Columbus took advantage of the Cincinnati loss with a 4-3 victory at Chicago to finish seventh and avoid the wild card round. At Miami, Messi’s 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte’s Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring. nigeria.title: Iran executes three men linked to anti-government protests
nigeria.description: Iranian authorities have executed three men convicted of carrying out operations on behalf of Israel and the United States during anti-government protests in January, the country’s judiciary has announced. The death sentences against Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were carried out on Sunday after being upheld by the Supreme Court, the judiciary’s Mizan Online website reported. According to the report, the three men were found guilty of “participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups” during the protests. Mizan said the defendants threw Molotov cocktails and grenades, used bladed weapons and firearms, and set fire to public facilities in Karaj, a city west of Tehran. Other defendants in the case received prison sentences ranging from five to 10 years, the report added. The protest movement, which initially erupted in December over the rising cost of living, rapidly developed into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on January 8 and 9. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths during the unrest, blaming the violence on what they described as “terrorist acts” orchestrated by the United States and Israel. However, foreign-based non-governmental organisations have reported higher casualty figures and maintained that Iranian security forces fired on protesters. The number of executions in Iran has increased since the outbreak of the Middle East war, which was triggered in late February by US and Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic. nigeria.title: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos forward, Oluebube Umejiaku, has explained how the team recovered from their opening defeat to Poland to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Nigeria began their campaign with a 2-1 loss to Poland, despite Umejiaku scoring as a substitute. However, the team bounced back, treating every subsequent fixture as a final on their way to winning the competition. The Flamingos defeated DPR Korea, Mexico and other opponents before overcoming Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to claim the trophy. Umejiaku, who started the tournament on the bench, became one of Nigeria’s standout performers, scoring crucial goals, including in the final, and winning the Golden Ball award as the tournament’s best player. Speaking to FIFA.com after Nigeria’s historic triumph, she said the players were determined to change their fortunes following the opening loss to Poland. “When we lost the first game against Poland, everybody said we needed to wake up because we didn’t come here to look at anybody’s face and we have to take every game as a final. We don’t downgrade anything; we play and we put all our best into every game.” Umejiaku also reflected on her journey from a substitute to one of the tournament’s most influential players, saying she remained hopeful of getting an opportunity to start. “Every time I went to training and every time I slept, I told God that I’m praying for all the people that are starting. But when I wanted to start, I just told God that it is my time,” she said. Another key contributor to Nigeria’s triumph was Awawu Bashiru, who initially had limited playing time under head coach Akeem Busari. Bashiru played just 77 minutes between the opening match and the quarter-final against Venezuela before earning her first start against Brazil. She scored twice in that encounter and also opened the scoring in the final against Japan. nigeria.title: Israeli president Herzog picks Eisenkot to form new government
nigeria.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition leader and former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, to form a new government following an election that left both his camp and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition short of a parliamentary majority. Herzog’s office announced on Saturday night that the president had informed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, of his intention to give him the mandate to form a government. The formal appointment is expected to take place at a ceremony at the president’s residence in Jerusalem on Sunday. “This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X following the announcement. The decision brings Eisenkot closer to replacing Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, after the religious-nationalist coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s camp secured 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc won 48, leaving both short of the 61 seats required to form a government. During consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received endorsements from two Arab-majority political lists, whose support could prove crucial in the coalition-building process. However, uncertainty remains over whether Eisenkot’s bloc would accept a formal alliance with the Arab-led parties, particularly after more than three years of war in Gaza. Netanyahu has opposed any arrangement involving the Arab parties, accusing them of supporting terrorism and warning against forming a government with what he described as “terrorist supporters”. He has also called for a national unity government. Eisenkot, however, has indicated a willingness to work with Arab-led parties under certain conditions, including their acceptance that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be dismantled. He has also pledged to take action against extremist Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank accused of attacking Palestinians, describing the incidents as “Jewish terror” allegedly enabled by Netanyahu’s government. Despite his willingness to engage with Arab-led parties, Eisenkot opposes the creation of a Palestinian state. He has also vowed to end Hamas’ rule in Gaza and destroy its military wing. Eisenkot served as Israel’s Chief of General Staff from 2015 to 2019 and commanded the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah. During the conflict, he developed the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”, a military strategy advocating the use of overwhelming force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by Hezbollah. Under the Israeli constitutional process, Eisenkot has 28 days to secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers and form a government. Herzog can grant him an additional 14 days if he fails to meet the deadline. If Eisenkot cannot secure a parliamentary majority within the allotted period, the president may offer the mandate to another candidate. Failure by any candidate to form a government

nigeria.title: WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) has renewed its push for greater participation of women in business and leadership, identifying mentorship, visibility and empowerment as key tools for helping women access opportunities and advance their careers. The Executive Head of WIMBIZ, Omowunmi Akingbohungbe, said the organisation was committed to inspiring and empowering women to attain leadership positions while equipping them to become entrepreneurs. Speaking during an interview at the organisation’s 25th annual conference in Lagos, Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ connects experienced and accomplished women with emerging leaders to guide them through the challenges of building careers and businesses. “We’re big on mentoring. We connect mentors, accomplished and experienced women with rising leaders so they can handhold them and show them the path so they’re not reinventing the wheel,” she said. She also stressed the importance of visibility, noting that women needed to make their abilities known, develop confidence and put themselves forward for leadership opportunities. According to her, many women often hold back from applying for leadership positions because they feel they are not qualified, whereas men are more likely to take the chance. “Most times women will think I’m not qualified and all of that, but men would apply. And we also have the potential,” she said. Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ was therefore working to ensure women recognise their capabilities and have the confidence to pursue opportunities in business and public service. “At WIMBIZ, we train, mentor, empower women. We give women a right to be entrepreneurs at the same time,” she added. She described the organisation’s partnership with Autos, its official automobile partner for the annual conference, as part of its 25th anniversary celebrations. She said the partnership would also provide discounts to WIMBIZ members and free vehicle servicing for two years. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. sports.title: Usman Khawaja says 'I haven't thrown anyone under the bus' after ball-tampering revelations
sports.description: Usman Khawaja has denied throwing anyone under the bus after making explosive claims about the infamous ‘Sandpaper-gate’ scandal in his new book. Khawaja, who retired after last winter’s Ashes, wrote in extracts in his autobiography Sabr , which is set to be published on Tuesday, that the entire Australia team knew about the plot to use sandpaper to tamper with the ball during a Test match against South Africa in Cape Town 2018. At the time only captain Steve Smith, deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught on television cameras applying the sandpaper, took responsibility for the scheme. The former two received one-year bans while Bancroft was suspended for nine months. Khawaja said that captain Steve Smith talked him out of insisting the entire team take responsibility and also alleged that a member of the coaching staff encouraged Bancroft. Khawaja said in a two-part video statement on Instagram: “I haven’t thrown anyone under the bus. These three guys took the blame for all of us and they’re the victims. The truth has never come out. “I stayed quiet yesterday but if you read my article you’d have seen, when I said it was all of us, that’s implying that whether we like it or not we are all responsible for what happened together. As a team, we need to take that collectively. Am I going to deny that everyone knew? No. “But I never speak on behalf of anyone else in my book – contrary to what the headlines in clickbait media would have you think. “The only other thing that I think is really relevant, which I want to talk about, is the question why now? Well, because I’ve been trying to take this as a team right from the start. You can believe my story or not.” Khawaja added: “When the other guys got their penalties I told Smudge (Smith) that I was going to come clean to the media. I couldn’t believe the penalty he got, but Smudge being the man and leader he was talked me out of it. “He wanted to take the blame. I argued with him, but he was having none of it.” Khawaja said “all of us” knew about the plot and said that he had again wanted to come clean in 2021, before a statement was released by now-captain Pat Cummins and the rest of the bowling unit, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon in which they denied any involvement. “I wasn’t going to go to war with those guys,” Khawaja said. As for why he had waited until now to finally speak out, he said: “Call me a chicken or whatever you want. I didn’t know how to do it because I was still in the team. I was always conscious of putting my team first, but I’m not in that team anymore. What I say now isn’t a reflection of them anymore.” The book is also expected to allege that the same tactic was first used in the previous Test at Gqeberha. Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann denied Khawaja’s claims of widespread knowledge of the plot, but acknowledged that ball-tampering was a “big part” of international cricket during the period. Australia's next two tries came after they got six again thanks to poor Samoa discipline. Jacob Preston burst under the posts on 15 minutes; 10 minutes later, joint-top World Cup scorer Tom Trbojevic scored his eighth try of the tournament, benefiting after Crichton reached into the ruck. sports.title: Late release, upright seam, heavy ball: Decoding Mohammed Shami’s sorcery
sports.description: Few bowlers possessed the ability to strip a batter of his technique, judgement, and ego like Mohammed Shami. The fast bowler from a nondescript village in Uttar Pradesh’s Sahaspur, which literally translates to the “land of courage”, bowled with a big heart, indefatigable spirit, and unmatched skill over 64 Tests. Former England captain Alastair Cook’s dismissal during the Visakhapatnam Test in 2016 was a case in point. Shami bowled a series of outswingers that forced Cook to play away from his body. On cue, he then delivered a perfect inswinger that jagged back sharply to sneak past Cook's defence and cannon onto the stumps. “It’s all in those beautiful wrists,” Shami’s childhood coach Badruddin Siddiqui told TOI. “The reason for his success was that he released the ball late and did not rush through his action. This helped him extract late swing off the track. With those malleable wrists, he made subtle changes at the point of release that batters found hard to pick,” the coach demystified Shami’s skill set. Like S Sreesanth, Shami possessed one of the most upright, God-gifted seam positions in world cricket. Shami was also a bit of a paradox because of the ability to make the old ball skid low while also hurling the ‘heavy ball’ that flew past the batter’s nose. The ‘heavy ball’ — the delivery that pitches shorter and reaches the batter quicker than expected, and hits the bat with extra force despite bowling from a relatively smooth, upright run-up — became Shami’s calling card on numerous overseas tours. The 2018 Johannesburg Test was a classic example: he dismantled South Africa, cruising at 124/1, for 177 to hand India a landmark 63-run win. Shami finished with figures of 5/28, unleashing his trademark ‘heavy ball’ on the spicy Wanderers pitch. At times, he could be erratic even when the conditions were loaded in his favour. But without any warning, he would return with a magical, match-altering spell against the run of play. This streak of unpredictability made Shami irresistible, and it was instrumental in India winning more matches abroad, especially under Virat Kohli’s captaincy. Shami was also a great senior, who passed on his art and tricks of the trade to youngsters. “I learnt a lot of things from him during my time in the IPL. sports.title: Deion Sanders contract buyout, salary at Colorado in 2026
sports.description: The Colorado Buffaloes continue to rack up inexcusable losses against winnable opponents, despite having a coach paid like one of the best in college football. Those two things typically go on for a long time without any resolution. Will Colorado part ways with Deion Sanders? Who knows, but with each passing loss, most recently a 20-10 defeat to Arizona State in Tempe, the answer to that question gets clearer. Results matter, and over the past two seasons, and truthfully for the better part of his four-year tenure aside from 2024 as head coach, the results have been nowhere close to good enough for the amount of resources poured into the program. For a few weeks now, fans have been wondering what it would take for Colorado to move on from Sanders. Well, it would cost a pretty penny. Deion Sanders' contract details In March 2025, Sanders signed a five-year, $54 million contract extension with Colorado that runs through the 2029 season. His base salary this year is $10.8 million, the fourteenth-highest salary in college football. Needless to say, Colorado is nowhere near the fourteenth-best team in the country, and even if the extension was not just for the on-field product, but also for what Sanders brought to the university and city, those boosts have died down as well. Sanders would make $11 million in 2027, $11 million in 2028 and $12 million in 2029 if he saw out the remaining three years of his deal. Deion Sanders' buyout details Like most coaches, Sanders buyout changes depending on whether he leaves or is fired. Colorado could also work out a deal with Sanders to lower his buyout if both sides want to part ways, but that seems least likely, especially in season. If Sanders is fired before the end of 2026, his buyout would be $25.5 million. In 2027, that number would decrease to $17.25 million. Sanders would owe Colorado $10 million if he left for another job before December 31, 2026. Can Colorado afford Deion Sanders' buyout? The biggest question remains whether Colorado could afford the nearly $26 million buyout, and the short answer is yes. If you factor in that Sanders would be paid around $34 million over the next three seasons if he stays, the buyout ($25.5 million) would actually save the university under $8.5 million ($2.8 million per year). The buyout plus hiring a new head coach at $4-4.5 million per year would be about $37.5-39 million, or about $1.5 million more per year over three seasons. A very doable number if that is the direction CU chooses. If you hire a coach with an even lower annual salary, say a current Group of Six coach, the change could cost less than $1 million a year. sports.title: What Steph Curry went and said in the Warriors locker room right after beating Magic 126-119
sports.description: Photo by Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images The Golden State Warriors were involved in a thriller against the Orlando Magic. Steve Kerr’s men dominated the first half, winning the first quarter by 12 and the second by four, thus going into the break with a 16-point lead. However, in the third quarter, the Magic outscored the Warriors by 17 points and took the lead. Steph Curry led the comeback in the fourth, and with the game tied at the buzzer, the two teams went to overtime. The Warriors won by seven points in the end, and although Curry was the star of the show, he was beyond impressed by his teammates. Steph Curry’s locker room message to Golden State Warriors teammates after beating Orlando Magic If you just look at the scores and Curry’s stat sheet, you would think that the 38-year-old led his side to victory once again. You wouldn’t be wrong to think that, but what was really interesting at the start of overtime was seeing Kerr leave both Curry and Draymond Green on the bench. That shocked everyone, but the players on the court for the first minute or so helped the Warriors to go up by four points. Curry and Green then came on to finish the job, but seeing the younger guys deliver at such a key moment of the game really impressed the 2022 NBA Finals MVP. After the game, Curry reportedly went to the locker room and heaped praise on his teammates for their performance against the Magic. “Steve Kerr says Steph Curry addressed the team in the locker room tonight to tell them how much he trusts this group and gave praise to the bench and depth,” Dalton Johnson reported live on X. In his press conference , Kerr said: “He spoke to the team after the game about the contributions of the bench, and he mentioned how much trust that he and the vets have in the young guys. “So, we’ve got a good thing going.” Curry is absolutely right to praise his teammates. Leaving him and Green out for the first minute could’ve easily backfired, but the fact that it didn’t shows the quality of the depth. That is one of the reasons why the Warriors have now won seven games in a row.

technology.title: Doom delivers five minutes of terminal violence on an IBM mainframe
technology.description: Can an IBM Z mainframe run Doom? Of course it can. The more interesting question is whether you can play it through a text terminal without ruining your eyesight. WND Software's browser demo connects to an IBM Z mainframe over SSH using its terminal emulator. Wojciech Graj's DOOM-ASCII supplies the text-based carnage, replacing conventional graphics with colored characters. There's no sound. It is, however, completely playable (although you might need to recalibrate your vision to work out what is going on, particularly with regard to distant objects). Sessions are limited to five minutes, with room for up to 50 simultaneous users, but we had no trouble getting in. ASCII also presented no issues once the game was in motion. This writer played the original shareware release on an Amstrad ALT386SX portable, so squinting at an indistinct demon felt reassuringly familiar. That Doom can be persuaded to run on an IBM Z mainframe is not particularly noteworthy. The code has turned up everywhere from databases to PCB designers . Even the humble Pi Pico was roped into the fun. Keeping the action playable through a text terminal is the more entertaining achievement. A year ago, an IBM consultant persuaded Doom to run on IBM Z and LinuxONE using VNC to bring the pixelated mayhem to life. Using a terminal emulator, while a neat demonstration of the capabilities of WND's software, is perhaps more an example of "because I can" masochism. It's undeniably an enjoyable way to burn through five minutes. No installation or login required – just a willingness to shoot at punctuation. ®

technology.title: Internet governance about to get its quadrennial stress test at ITU meeting
technology.description: The International Telecommunications Union (ITU) kicks off its quadrennial plenipotentiary on Monday, and internet governance organizations are bracing in case the event becomes a forum for nation-states to try to challenge their roles. The ITU is the United Nations' specialized agency for information and communication technologies, meaning its members are nation-states. The body's role is to facilitate international connectivity, which it does by managing radio spectrum, satellite orbits, and working on relevant technical standards. Its key standards are pervasive. ITU-T X.509 sets out the rules of public key infrastructure. ITU-T E.164 governs telephone numbers. ITU-T H.264 and 265 define the video codecs used for most online streams. The ITU's role is largely uncontested, yet its work gets very close to that of the organizations who work on technologies that make the internet work. Those bodies include the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF); the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), which oversees the domain name system; and the regional internet registries (RIRs), which manage IP addresses. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) works on HTML, CSS, and accessibility. Governments participate in work at those internet governance bodies but are just one voice among many and can't override the consensus-driven decision-making process they use, under a system which has come to be known as the multi-stakeholder governance model. At a 2025 event called WSIS+20, the United Nations endorsed multi-stakeholder governance by deciding that its Internet Governance Forum (IGF) should become a permanent body. That decision effectively endorsed multi-stakeholder governance, and kept the ITU out of internet standards. Yet the IGF hasn't met since WSIS+20, so it is yet to start operating meaningfully as a permanent body. This year's ITU meeting is therefore a moment at which stakeholders can stress-test the delicate balance between the ITU, internet governance bodies, and the emerging IGF. Such a test could see ITU members try to have it pursue new fields that overlap with work performed by internet governance organizations. This has already happened before. China tried to have the ITU work on " New IP" – a major revision to internet protocol, a technology the IETF manages. In 2022, Russia and China backed a candidate for the ITU presidency who favored giving nations a stronger role in internet governance, potentialy by having the ITU take over some standards work. That candidate was not elected. Ahead of next week's meetings, the Internet Society published a background paper that declared it is "actively challenging proposals that could affect the Internet's underlying technical architecture or increase fragmentation, as well as those that could affect connectivity, particularly for remote, underserved, and unserved communities." science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history?
